data.say: Fixes made: the blade thrown at the monk (p160 "kozuka drawn from his sword") is now distinct from the small knife used underwater, since the Japanese has two different words (刀の小柄; 小刀) and the continuity of which blade Kotora later picks up depends on it; "as plain as if close at hand" (p127), Japanese 手に取るように, replaces "beside us", which invented a first-person narrator; "Guilty though the men they bound may have been" (p118) restores the concession in 罪有る者とは云え, which "Guilty men or no" reversed; "bunkin high shimada" (p144) now matches the same Japanese term's first rendering; "water-caltrops" (p154) now matches the 菱 rendering used a page later, so the man-eating weeds read as one plant; "Anego" (p54, p57) now matches the first rendering of 姉御 in this scene, so Ryūjirō's address to O-Tetsu does not change mid-conversation; and "handed down from master to master alone" (p4) restores 一家相伝, the one-master-to-one-disciple transmission the book's master-and-disciple theme turns on, where "his house" suggested a family line. The rope catalogues, the ferry mechanism, the dream essay, the rumour as rumour, the poison as suspicion, Kotora's flat stabbing with no death stated, and the circles and shrug of the coda are all as the Japanese leaves them.
data.verdict: Ready: the English says what the Japanese says, the rope vocabulary and the binding network hold consistently to the last page, Ryūjirō stays passive and stripped as the text makes him, and the ending is left as abrupt and unresolved as it is written.
